title: Bar-transfer principle: one-sided bounds on bar-invariant properties extend for free
html:
Proposition. Bar-transfer principle: one-sided bounds on bar-invariant properties extend for free

Let P \colon \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathrm{Prop} be a bar-invariant property of the substrate parameter:

  \forall\,q > 0,\quad P(q) \iff P(q^{-1}).

For every a > 0:

  1. Lower bound transfer. \bigl(\forall q > a,\; P(q)\bigr) \iff \bigl(\forall q < a^{-1},\, q > 0 \Rightarrow P(q)\bigr).

  2. Two-sided extension. If a < 1 and \bigl(\forall q \in (a, a^{-1}),\, P(q)\bigr), then \bigl(\forall q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} \setminus \{a, a^{-1}\},\, P(q)\bigr) does not follow in general. If P is continuous on \mathbb{R}_{>0}, bar-invariance forces P to extend symmetrically across both endpoints.

  3. Negation transfer. \bigl(\exists q < a,\, q > 0 \land \neg P(q)\bigr) \iff \bigl(\exists q > a^{-1},\, \neg P(q)\bigr).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at q_0. Categorical or q-deformation identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation requires specialisation here.
